contrasts.line: Startled lasts a moment; terrified is huge fear that can make you scream.
Startled is a quick reaction; timid is a shy pattern around people or new tasks.
Horrified is upset at an awful sight. Startled is the quick jump at a sudden one.
Terrified is huge and lasting; startled is a one-second jolt.
Terrified is extreme fear right now; timid is a shy way someone often acts.
Horrified is disgusted shock. Terrified is deep fear of real danger.
Timid is a usual shy manner; startled is a quick jolt.
Timid is gentle shyness; terrified is the strongest scare.
Horrified is one big shocked moment. Timid is being shy of things all the time.
Startled is the jump at something sudden. Horrified is the upset at something awful.
Terrified is the strongest FEAR of danger. Horrified is shock and disgust, not danger.
Timid is how someone always is. Horrified is a reaction to one awful sight.
Alarmed means spotting real danger and acting; startled is the jump before thinking.
Alarmed is quick, sensible worry at a danger sign; terrified is fear so big you can barely move.
Alarmed is a reaction to one danger sign; timid is being shy and careful all the time.
Alarmed is about danger coming; horrified is shock at something awful you see.
Startled is the flinch at a sudden surprise; alarmed is noticing danger and acting on it.
Terrified is overwhelming fear; alarmed is milder, a warning feeling that says check this now.
Timid describes a shy, careful nature; alarmed is one moment of spotting danger.
Horrified is shock at an awful sight; alarmed is concern that danger is on the way.
